hints: Notice $u = 0$, $v = 85 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ and $s = 1.20 \text{ km}$ must both be converted to SI units of $\text{m s}^{-1}$ and $\text{ m}$ before using a SUVAT equation.
Connect zero initial velocity and constant acceleration over a known distance to $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$, which rearranges to $a = v^2/(2s)$.
First calculate $85 \times 1000/3600$ to get $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, then square it and divide by $2 \times 1200$ to check the size of $a$ in $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: Identify the motion: $u = 0$, final speed $v = 85 \text{ km h}^{-1}$, displacement $s = 1.20 \text{ km}$ for the limiting minimum acceleration case.
Convert to SI units: $v = 85 \times 1000/3600 = 23.6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $s = 1.20 \times 1000 = 1200 \text{ m}$.
State the governing equation for constant acceleration with no time given: $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$.
Rearrange with $u = 0$ to $a = v^2/(2s)$ and substitute: $a = (23.6)^2/(2 \times 1200)$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $(23.6)^2 = 557 \text{ m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}$, so $a = 557/2400 = 0.23 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ with correct units.
